name: Chicago Midway International Airport
before:
Chicago's other airport, twelve miles from the Loop on the south west side, and often the better choice for a client who wants to be in the city quickly. The CTA Orange Line runs from the terminal straight downtown.

Southwest Airlines carries more than 90 per cent of the passengers here, so this is the airport to price when a client is flying Southwest. It handled 22,050,489 passengers in 2023, second in Illinois after O'Hare.

The constraint is space. The whole airport fits into just over one square mile, boxed in by streets on all four sides, and the city has grown right up to the fence. The runways are short by big airport standards, the longest being 6,522 feet, and the landing thresholds are displaced to clear obstacles, so aircraft have less runway available for landing than for take off.

Midway opened in 1927 and was Chicago's main airport until O'Hare opened in 1944. It is named after the Battle of Midway. The current terminal was completed in 2001 with 43 gates.
after:
Chicago's other airport, about eight miles south west of the Loop and often the better choice for a client who wants to be in the city quickly. The CTA Orange Line runs straight downtown from beside the terminal.

Southwest Airlines carries about 90 per cent of the passengers here, so this is the airport to price when a client is flying Southwest. It handled about 19.4 million passengers in 2025, second in Illinois after O'Hare.

Space is the constraint. The whole airport fits into just over one square mile, surrounded by city neighbourhoods. Its runways are short by big airport standards, the longest being 6,522 feet.

Midway was dedicated in 1927 and was Chicago's main airport until the early 1960s, when the airlines moved to O'Hare. It is named after the Battle of Midway. The current terminal building opened in 2001, and there are 43 gates.

claims.claim: Chicago's main airport until the early 1960s, when the airlines moved to O'Hare
claims.inAfter: was Chicago's main airport until the early 1960s, when the airlines moved to O'Hare
claims.note: Was 'until O'Hare opened in 1944', copied from Wikipedia's opening paragraph, which its own history section contradicts. Passenger service at O'Hare began in 1955; O'Hare passed Midway by 1961 and United, the last airline, left Midway in 1962 (CDA); O'Hare's new terminal opened in 1962 and the airlines consolidated there (Wikipedia).

quote: In 1955, passenger service began at O'Hare
By 1961, commercial flights at O'Hare soared past Midway causing it to relinquish the "World's Busiest Airport" title.
United Airlines, the first airline to institute service at Midway, was now the last to move out, with its last flight departing to Toledo, Ohio, in 1962.
